With single-minded devotion, I invoke the talented and eminent scholars of the five imperial tombs and the virtuous and worthy men of the hundred prefectures—those who have served with pure integrity for three years and who repay their sovereign with a heart as crimson as cinnabar.
(Prose: From the southern provinces to the northern counties, long separated from the homelands of our native villages; from the ends of the earth to the furthest reaches of the heavens.
Far away, they have lost their way on the island of Penglai. (Alas! Their official circumstances are desolate, following the passing waters;
their wandering souls are distant, separated by the Yang Pass. Such are the ranks of civil officials and high ministers—a multitude of solitary spirits of this kind.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke the talented scholars of the academy and the students from humble dwellings: those who have trodden the paths of the literary groves as they sought the Plumeria Blossom, and those whose bodies have journeyed to the halls of the *Ji* (the imperial examination) by means of the *she-ce* (policy essays).
(Interlude) The glowworm lamps flicker out; three years of labor were in vain. The iron inkstone has been worn through.
In ten years of labor spent in vain—(Alas!)—seven feet of crimson silk inscribe one’s name, while a mound of yellow earth covers one’s literary talent.
Such as these, the ranks of scholars and men of letters, along with all classes of solitary spirits.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke: the transcendent masters who have emerged from the dust, the high monks with flying staffs, the pure practitioners who have refined the five precepts, and the assembly of bhikṣuṇīs of holy conduct.
(Recite: Amidst yellow chrysanthemums and verdant bamboos, we discuss in vain the secret, true expositions; even the white oxen and tawny slaves [partake in this].
In vain they recite the wondrous verses on suffering and emptiness. (Alas! Through the window of the sutra-chamber, the cold moon of the third watch is reflected;
within the meditation hall, the empty clarity of the midnight lamp shines. Such are the ranks of the black-robed sons of Śākya, this assembly of a class of awakened spirits.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke those who wear yellow caps as rustic hermits and those in feathered robes as immortals. They cultivate the Way within the Peach Blossom Spring and nurture their nature before the islands of Langyuan.
(Recite: Though they have practiced the Three Flowers and Nine Refinements, the Celestial Bureaus have not yet permitted them to record their names; for the Four Elements are impermanent.
The Netherworld finds it difficult to grant further extensions of one's term. (Alas! At Linguan, the frost is cold and the alchemical hearths are chill;
at the altar of the incantation, the wind is bleak and the apricot blossoms are sparse. Such are the ranks of the Daoist masters of the Mysterious Gate and the various classes of distant spirits.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke you: those bound by travel upon rivers and lakes, merchants journeying north and south, wandering ten thousand *li* in pursuit of wealth, and trading with thousands of pieces of gold in accumulated goods.
(Recite: The winds and frost are unpredictable; one’s body may be smeared within the belly of a fish. The roads are difficult to guard against; [may there be no harm].
Their lives were lost on the treacherous path of Yangchang. (Alas! Their lingering spirits follow the clouds northward in gloom;
their souls as guests pursue the waters eastward in vast expanse. Such are the multitudes of solitary spirits among the streams of travelers from distant lands.
With single-minded resolve, he summons the soldiers in their armor and the valiant warriors facing the fray. Amidst the shadows of red banners they vie for supremacy;

amidst the clusters of white blades they risk their lives. (Prose: As the drums and gongs first resound, in an instant their bellies are ripped open and their entrails pierced. Victory and defeat are then divided.
Everywhere limbs are mangled and heads are shattered. (Alas! Vast stretches of yellow sand resound with the wailing of ghosts;
boundless white bones remain largely uncollected. Such are the ranks of soldiers fallen in battle, this multitude of solitary spirits.

With single-minded devotion, he summoned the beautiful maidens of the inner chambers and the exquisite ladies of the private quarters; their faces vied for beauty with rouge and paint, and their garments contended for elegance with the scent of dragon’s brain and musk.
(Prose: The clouds have gathered and dispersed; their souls have vanished from the gardens of Jingu. The moon is waning and the flowers are withered.
My intestines break at the post station of Mawei. (Alas! Of the elegance of former days, not a trace remains. Amidst green willows and fragrant grasses, cold skulls lie scattered.
Such as these—the classes of women with their skirts and hairpins, and the multitudes of solitary spirits alike.

With single-minded devotion, she invoked [the spirit]. She carried him in her womb for ten months and sat upon the grass for three days. First, she rejoiced at the harmonious cries of the phoenix and the peacock;

next, she looked forward to the auspicious dreams of the bear and the cubs. (Statement: We respectfully wish to sing [the praises]; fortune and misfortune depend on but a moment. Whether it be a precious jade or a broken tile remains undivided.
Mother and child alike return to the long night. (Alas! When the flowers are in full bloom, they encounter a torrential rain; when the moon is at its brightest, it is shrouded by dark clouds.
Such is the fate of those in the Blood Lake who suffer the perils of childbirth, and of the various classes of solitary spirits.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke those from the lands of the Man, Yi, Rong, and Di; the mute, the dumb, the blind, and the deaf; the laborers who lose their lives for others, and the servants and concubines whose bodies are wounded by jealousy.
(Recite: Those who have slighted and deceived the Triple Gem, whose transgressions and sins accumulate like the sands of the Ganges, and those who have been unfilial toward their parents.
Villainy floats throughout the universe. (Alas! The long night stretches on; when will it dawn? The dark gates remain hidden;
one knows not of spring. Such are the masses of solitary spirits—those who are obstinate, perverse, and rebellious.

With single-minded devotion, I invoke those who were hungry and cold beggars, prisoners subjected to execution, those who perished in water or fire, and those who lost their lives encountering tigers and wolves.
(Recite: Those who hanged themselves or took poison—their vengeful spirits linger for a thousand years; those struck by lightning or buried under collapsing cliffs.
A trace of lingering terror stirs. (Alas! In the evening rain and blue smoke, cold magpies shriek; in the autumn wind and yellow leaves, crows fly in disorder.
Such are those who have met with injury or death by violence, and the various classes of solitary spirits.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke all those within the five realms of the Dharma-realm, the ten classes of orphaned spirits, and the vast multitudes of *pīlī* ghosts under their jurisdiction—
beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who cling to grass and wood, *chīmèi* and *wǎngliǎng* demons, lingering souls and solitary spirits,
and all deceased ancestors and kinsmen, both one’s own and others’. I pray that you will, by virtue of this invocation, accept...
By the power of the Triple Gem and relying upon secret mantras, you have now arrived at this assembly this very night to receive this unobstructed nectar of Dharma-food.
Since all those invited above have now arrived, may the great assembly, out of compassion, join their voices in lamentation.
I bow my head in refuge to the Hero, whose golden countenance dwells like the moon in water. On the shores of Jambudvīpa, he exercises vast compassion with great weight.
He has made the great vow to deliver all from the cage of worldly bondage. Amitābha’s precious crown and jeweled necklaces rest upon his head, adorned with exquisite, shimmering flowers.
The three calamities and eight difficulties—upon hearing this voice, their sufferings are rescued. Shackles, fetters, and stocks are transformed into a pure breeze.
Precious jewels are scattered to universally relieve the poor. From within his hand, he sprinkles the ambrosia of the *śītalā* branch from time to time, moistening the throats of the deceased.
We pray that this very night, at this Dharma assembly, you will receive and guide the departed spirits upward to the celestial palaces.
Namo Bubudeti-likālidali-tadūyathāya-jian-wang-sheng-pusa-mohe-sa-tan-gu.
The Secret Words of the Awakened Sovereign enliven the Imperial Capital; where is there that the great propagation of the Patriarchal Wind does not reach?
A single day’s auspicious air pervades the stars and constellations, while the myriad phenomena radiate brilliance upon the incense burners.
May those of the four modes of birth be guided to the nine grades of purity, and may those of the six realms be led forth from the three miserable paths.
At this moment, fortunately encountering a fine night’s gathering, the bells and chimes resound together, evoking sighs for the solitary state of former eras.
The imperial majesty and honorable rank of past sovereigns, the nobility and princely lineage of dukes and kings, the high officials and ladies of the inner court,
and the various classes of palace attendants and consorts— all have their dreams severed in the realm of Huaxu, now coming to receive the flavor of sweet nectar.
A statesman and court minister, who had woven the threads of governance to rectify the age and governed the common people, failed to fulfill his loyal and virtuous aspirations.
Having lost favor and harboring sorrow, he was banished to a frontier land; yet with his soul lingering in longing for his country, he has now come to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.
Generals and military officers, commanding three divisions of troops, drew up battle arrays and clashed in combat; the sound of gongs and drums resounded through heaven and earth.

Fighting in the north and campaigning in the south, they perished upon the desolate fields of war. Having sacrificed their lives for the sake of the nation, they now come to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.

Studying the ancients and exhausting the Classics, you were a scholar whose writings were like brocade and embroidery. Illuminating the snow and stealing the light, you applied yourself with bitter resolve within the cold window.
Yet fate has slipped by, and your name is not upon the golden scroll. Now, as a sorrowful spirit, come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

Renouncing what is dear and bidding farewell to kin, he entered the gates of the Empty Gate early on. Seeking the Way and searching for a teacher was solely for the purpose of transcending birth and death.

As heat passes and cold arrives, one fails to realize impermanence; yet, through the turning back of reflection and the returning of light, one comes to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Clad in feathered robes and wearing yellow caps, you set out early with the resolve to cultivate the truth. You refine elixirs and burn cinnabar, nourishing your nature to restore the primal qi.
Through asceticism and mental toil, you hope to ascend to the rank of an immortal. Do not cling to this decaying form; come instead to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.

Filial sons and worthy grandsons, men of righteousness, valor, loyalty, and goodness; virtuous women and faithful wives—regarding death as returning home, they uphold their integrity and sacrifice their bodies, leaving behind heroic spirits for a thousand ages.
May their resolute souls come now to partake of the flavor of the sweet nectar.
The female monastics of the Way dwell in bodies upon the ground of golden light; like phoenixes soaring through the void, they are untainted by worldly affairs.
Having not yet realized the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), they wander through the cycle of empty birth and death. May these pure spirits come now to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

Whether through geography and astronomy, the categories of medicine and yin-yang, divination by hexagrams or tortoise shells, physiognomy, or the astrologers who announce auspiciousness and speak of misfortune—one cannot avoid impermanence.
One must abandon the false and return to the True, coming to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Those who engage in various enterprises as sitters-at-home merchants or traveling traders, possessing many skills in arts and crafts and trade to seek wealth and profit,
leaving their wells and villages to die in foreign lands— their wanderings in dreams are long and vast— now come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Those who have violated the law and suffered punishment, those long confined in dark prisons, those bound for their lives by schemes, those burdened by creditors, and those with karmic enemies;
those afflicted by swellings, poisons, and epidemics, and those who died of cold or hunger—may you swiftly depart from the Yellow Springs and come to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.
Those mangled by chariots, those with bodies trampled by horses, those crushed by collapsing walls or falling cliffs, those who committed suicide by slashing their throats or hanging from beams,

those burned or swept away by water and fire, and those bitten by tigers or harmed by snakes— may these solitary spirits of the nine untimely deaths come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Drinking blood and eating raw fur, they were born and raised in the lands of the barbarians; burdened by debt and labor, they became concubines, handmaidens, and slaves.
Mute, blind, deaf, and crippled, with no one to rely upon—may these suffering and grievous spirits come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
They were defiant toward their parents; they reviled Heaven and Earth; they slandered the Buddhas and deceived the Sangha; they destroyed images and burned sutras and verses.
Fallen into the deep pit of false views, their bitter retribution was boundless. May these frantic spirits of the ten evil deeds now come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

The Great Gate of Giving is opened. May those among the solitary spirits, our ancestors and deceased kin, and the various classes of karmic enemies, all equally transcend the eight difficulties and the three miserable realms.
Relying on the Buddha’s radiant light for deliverance, come now to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

Amitābha Buddha has long possessed boundless vows. Beholding sentient beings constantly drifting and drowning in the sea of suffering, he extends his hand with earnest compassion, specifically launching the vessel of mercy to rescue them.
He universally carries all beings across, so they may together attend the assembly at the Lotus Pond.
*Namo* to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the Lotus Pond Assembly.

By the power of my great compassion and the Buddha’s spiritual might, I summon all sentient beings of the dark and light realms, including the hungry ghosts who have been parched with hunger for kalpas; do not disobey the Buddha’s command, but descend here!

Next, form the mudrā for summoning hungry ghosts (the left hand forms the gesture of fearlessness; the right hand is held upright with the fingers slightly bent forward, the fourth finger [ring finger] extended).
[The Hook (Aṅkuśa). Recite the mantra:
Oṃ jvala-jvālaya he he svāhā. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as before.
One should visualize the white syllable Hrīḥ being emitted from the hand-mudrā of the left hand.)
The light hooks those ghost hosts and brings them to the site of practice (bodhimaṇḍa). They circumambulate the Buddha three times, pay homage to him, and depart for the area outside the altar.

The area outside the altar is divided into four gates: from the eastern gate to the southern gate are the hosts of hell-beings; from the southern gate to the southwest corner are the hosts of hungry ghosts;
from the southwest corner to the western gate are the hosts of animals; and from the western gate to the northwest corner are humans.
The assembly: from the northwest corner to the north gate, the asura hosts; from the north gate to the east gate, the deva hosts.
They should be stationed in this manner. The attendant said: "This is for the sake of providing comfort."

Once the invitation has been made, they all assemble like clouds; with a heart of compassion, he praises and consoles them, causing them to rejoice, and then [the cymbals are struck] to signal their thirsty longing for the Dharma.
Welcome, O Sons of the Buddha! Because you have previously formed superior karmic connections, you now encounter this auspicious assembly; do not give rise to anxiety or fear.
With single-minded longing for the Dharma, do not let this moment pass by. Let the precepts be moistened upon your bodies, so that you may swiftly depart from the realms of suffering.
"O you sons of the Buddhas, having encountered this place of enlightenment, all your various sins shall be summoned into the Vajra Fist.

Next, form the mudrā for summoning sins (with both hands in the vajra-bind, extend the ring fingers like needles, and bend the index fingers like hooks). The mantra for summoning sins is as follows: [Insert Mantra].
Oṃ sarvabuddhasamayasambhava-jñānasattva-samaya hūṃ. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly.
One should visualize a white syllable Hrīḥ upon the tips of the two middle fingers.)
The syllable *Kṣa* emits light and enters into that body, causing its transgressions to emerge like a mass of smoke and mist. He asks: "Transgressions have no substantial reality;
why do you now say they emerge like smoke and mist as if they possessed substantial reality? He replies: "Although they have no [substantial reality]..."
(The substance [of these sins] fills heaven and earth and obstructs the eyes and mind, preventing one from perceiving the pure realm of all Buddhas.
Now, by using mists as the object of focus (*ālambana*), we summon the actuality of those sins; this will be beneficial for the task at hand.)
All evil karmic deeds of sin are destroyed, Just as they are extinguished by the fire at the end of an eon. When the fire is extinguished, there remains only vajra-dust;

Next, form the mudrā for destroying sins (with the eight fingers crossed inwardly, the thumbs and ring fingers extended like needles). Then recite the mantra for destroying sins: *Vajra-tuṣita-samaya hūṃ phaṭ* (or according to the specific tradition: *Oṃ vajra-kīlaya sarvapāpān nāśaya hūṃ phaṭ*) (Note: The specific mantra varies by tradition; the above is a representative form.)
Oṃ vajrapāṇi-mūṣṭi-puthaje sarvāpad-vyapana-nī-pramocaye sarvāpad-gati-vyaparaka sarvasattvān sarvatrātāgata-vat.
*Jraḥ samaya hūṃ traṭ*. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as follows:
at the tips of the two middle fingers, visualize the syllable *tra* on the left and the syllable *ṭa* on the right.
The practitioner should cause their own body to increase and visualize themselves as the greenish-blue Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.)
With one's body, recite the mantra once for each repetition. Rub and shake the two middle fingers; upon reaching the final repetition, clap the hands to make a sound.
Visualize that mountain of sins collapsing like a stack of earthenware tiles. As for the previously summoned sins that were like smoke and mist, they shall disperse instantly upon this thought.
Question: Since sin has no substance or form, how can it be crushed? Answer: It is precisely because it is non-existent.
Therefore, it is crushed. If it were determinately existent, how could it be crushed?
Through the power of the empowerment of samādhi, even karmic deeds of fixed necessity and all obstacles and difficulties from beginningless time are entirely extinguished.

Next, perform the mudrā for destroying obstructive karma (with the two hands in the vajra-palms gesture; bend the second joints of the index fingers [vajra-arms]; press the ring fingers [dhyāna] and middle fingers [prajñā] at their second joints to destroy obstructive karma). The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrakarma-cuḍāmaṇi-sarvāvaraṇaviśodhani-buddhasatye samaya hūṃ.
(The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly. Visualize a blue syllable Hrīḥ arising from the moon disc at the heart.)

Guang (Light) summoned the assembly of ghosts before him and said: "Regarding all karmic actions that are not cleared through repentance by the Buddhas, one should contemplate that their self-nature is pure and fundamentally non-existent.
One should contemplate and observe that there is no difference between those ghosts, the Buddhas, and one's own mind.
This is called 'breaking determinate karma. This single method is precisely for severing the cognitive obscuration (*jñeyāvaraṇa*); let the students know this. [End of] Attendant.
The white-robed one said:
"The nature of sin is fundamentally empty, created by the mind; when the mind is extinguished, sin likewise perishes.
When sin perishes and the mind is extinguished, both are empty—this is what is called true repentance."

Next, form the mudrā for repentance and the eradication of sins (with the two hands in vajra-bond, the six fingers interlaced externally; bend the second joints of the thumbs and forefingers, snap the thumbs, and press down the two index fingers).
Then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ sphoṭa taha vajriye svāhā. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly.
One should visualize the syllable HŪṂ, white in color, upon the two bent fingers.)

Entering that ghost’s body, it is like the sun melting away dew; the defilements of sin are dissolved and melted away like ink, flowing down from the feet and seeping into the earth until reaching the adamantine foundation (*vajra-pṛthivī*). He asks: "Since you have previously summoned them, and they have been crushed and shattered."

Now, he performs repentance once again. Why? The answer is: what preceded was entirely repentance on the level of principle (*li*); now, for the first time, it is repentance on the level of phenomena (*shi*).
Since principle and phenomena are non-obstructive (*wǎngài*), there is no confusion between them. Again, he asks: "What kind of sin is like ink? The answer is:
"Sin" refers to black karma (*kṛṣṇa-karman*). Therefore, ink is used to represent it; because it has the meaning of flowing and spreading, it is so called.
It is like ink; one uses phenomena to manifest the principle, but must not become mired in them).
O Sons of the Buddha, having already performed repentance, the sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are instantly and completely swept away.
Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished utterly, leaving nothing behind.
A single drop of cool water can remove hunger, thirst, and fever; by sprinkling it upon the gate of the crown, it brings peace and happiness to all.
Next, form the *Amṛta-dāna-mudrā* (Nectar-bestowing Seal) of the Tathāgata of Wondrous Form (*Suvarṇa-kāya*). (According to the Guan-zang edition, the sequence of hand gestures is used throughout.)

The right hand [is joined with] either the *śīla-pāramitā* (morality) and *dhyāna-pāramitā* (meditation), or the *kṣānti-pāramitā* (patience) and *dhyāna-pāramitā*, or the *vīrya-pāramitā* (diligence) and *dhyāna-pāramitā*. As for the two-hand mudrā of the Tathāgata Subhavarṇa, it uses the power of the left hand to cause the *prajñā-pāramitā* (wisdom) and [the other hand] to snap together;
thus, according to the Tibetan manuscript, it is also called the "Seal of Bestowing Coolness."
*Namo surupaye dhatadaye tatte taṃ oṃ suru suru prasu ru prasu ru svāhā.* (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly.
Form the mudrā and recite the mantra while visualizing a white syllable *vaṃ* upon the palm of the right hand.)
The syllable emits nectar, the color of mercury, which is produced by true wisdom. (With the power and wisdom of the left hand, take a drop.
(Sprinkle it into the void, visualizing that all classes of devas, humans, ghosts, and others touch this nectar, whereby they all become fully endowed with physical form and characteristics.)
The fierce fires are extinguished; all attain refreshing coolness. Free from hunger and thirst, the conceptualizations of the mind’s grasping and its terrors are extinguished.
You all, since immeasurable kalpas past, have created various evil karmas and given rise to stinginess and greed;
by the power of this karma, your throats were closed, but by relying on this secret mantra, they are all opened and made passable.
Next, perform the mudrā for opening the throat (the master’s mudrā and mantra are as previously known). One should visualize a blue lotus flower within the palm of the left hand.

Upon the flower, visualize a white letter *A* from which flows the water of intrinsic nature, exceedingly pure and cool. Taking some with the right hand, snap the fingers and sprinkle it into the void.
[Visualize emptiness. Imagine that all the hosts of spirits are able to touch this water; their throats become vast, cool, moist, and unobstructed.
[Question: Previously, the syllable *hrīḥ* was used extensively; why is this syllable used alone here? What is the reason? [Answer:
The syllable *A* is the seed-syllable of speech; therefore, it is employed according to the three root tantras.

Oṃ namo bhagavate śrī-prajñāpāramitāyai. O sons of the Buddha, now that I have performed the mudrā and mantra for you, your throats shall open of their own accord, and you shall attain unimpeded penetration.
Free from all obstacles and difficulties, O sons of the Buddha, I now extol for you the auspicious name of the Tathāgata,
which shall enable you to forever leave behind the sufferings of the three evil realms and the eight difficult conditions, and to always be true and pure sons of the Tathāgata.

Namo Ratnasambhava Tathāgata (With the two hands in the vajra-palms mudrā, the six perfections in the inner-facing crossed position, the thumbs touching at their tips, and the ring and middle fingers standing upright on their sides; all sentient beings together recite the sacred name).
Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnottama! Sons of the Buddha,
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnottama, it shall cause the fires of the karma of your afflictions to be entirely extinguished.

Namo Vibhīṣaṇavigata-tathāgatāya (Right hand raised at the chest; the fingers of patience and meditation are joined. The left palm is turned upward and hanging down with the five fingers extended. Recite the mantra as follows).
Homage to the Tathāgata Vighnāntakṛt! O sons of the Buddha,
if you hear this name of the Tathāgata, it shall cause you all to always attain peace and happiness,
forever free from alarm and fear, and endowed with pure joy.

Namo to Vipula-kāya Tathāgata (The left hand, with the fingers curved inward toward the palm, strikes the shoulders with the thumb and index finger; the right hand, in the vajra-palm mudrā, strikes the chest with the thumbs and middle fingers).

*Namo bhagavate vipulaśarīra-tathāgatāya*. O sons of the Buddhas, if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Vipulaśarīra, it shall cause the fire of karma to cease burning within your needle-throated hungry ghosts, so that you may attain refreshing clarity;
and whatever food and drink you receive shall take on the taste of nectar (*amṛta*).

Namo to the Tathāgata of Wondrous Form (The left hand is held upright at the chest; the fingers of power and wisdom snap against one another. The right hand is curved and extended; the palm is turned upward and lowered).
Homage to the sons of the Buddhas, such as Surūpāyatagatagataya.
If you hear the name of the Tathāgata Wonderful Form Body (Surūpa-kāya), it shall cause you not to undergo ugliness,
but to possess all sense faculties in full, with the marks and signs of perfection complete, most excellent and dignified, becoming the foremost among those in the heavens and the human realm.
First: Namo to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna. (Join the two palms together in the void in the shape of a lotus. Namo Bhagavate Ratnārciṣe.
O sons of the Buddha, if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, it will enable you to be fully endowed with wealth and treasures,
so that whatever you require shall be obtained according to your wishes, and your enjoyments shall be inexhaustible.
Namo Amitābha Tathāgata (press the right wing over the left wing; the marks of wisdom support one another).
Namo Amitābhāya Tathāgatāya. O sons of the Buddha:
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha, it can cause you all to be reborn in the Western [Pure Land].
To the Land of Ultimate Bliss, one is born by transformation from a lotus flower and enters the stage of non-retrogression.
*Namo* to the Tathāgata Vast and Great Majestic Virtue Sovereign Radiance of the World. (Right hand: extend the little finger and form a fist; snap the fingers of the patience and dhyāna fingers.)
Turn the left palm upward, extend the five fingers, and recite the secret mantra: *Namo lokavidyeśvarāya dīptacintāmaṇiratnāya*.
O sons of the Buddha, if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Vast and Magnificent Sovereign Radiance, it will enable you to obtain five kinds of merit: first, being the most supreme among all worlds;
second, obtaining a Bodhisattva body that is dignified and exceptionally sublime; third, possessing vast majesty and virtue that surpasses—
All non-Buddhists and celestial Māras [are eclipsed], like the sun illuminating the world, manifesting the towering majesty of the great ocean of merit.
Fourth, one attains great sovereignty; wherever one turns, it is as one wishes, like a bird flying through the sky without obstruction.
Fifth, one attains great, firm wisdom; the body and mind are luminous and transparent, like a crystal bead.

"O sons of the Buddha! These seven Tathāgatas, by the power of their vows, rescue sentient beings, causing them to forever leave behind afflictions and escape the sufferings of the three miserable realms, abiding in peace, security, and eternal bliss.
By reciting their names even once, one shall be free from suffering for a thousand lifetimes and realize the Unsurpassed Way.
(Having thus made these three proclamations, the presiding master strikes the sounding block.)
Next, I take refuge in the Triple Gem with you all.
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire;
I take refuge in the Sangha, the Honored One among assemblies. By taking refuge in the Buddha, one does not fall into hell.
By taking refuge in the Dharma, one does not fall among the hungry ghosts. By taking refuge in the Saṅgha, one does not fall among the animals.
O children of the Buddha, you have completed your refuge in the Buddha, completed your refuge in the Dharma, and completed your refuge in the Saṅgha.
Because I take refuge in the Triple Gem, I shall firmly uphold the Dharma according to the teachings; Having myself departed from the path of false views, I therefore pay homage with a sincere heart.

Next, form the Seal of the Triple Gem (the left hand forms a fist; extend the index finger and place it at the chest; with the right hand, bend the middle finger and recite the mantra of the Triple Gem). The mantra of the Triple Gem is: *Namo ratnatrayāya* (Homage to the Triple Gem).
Oṃ bā (reduplicated) kaṃ.
Homage to the Buddha. Homage to the Dharma.
Homage to the Saṅgha. I now resolve:
The mind does not seek for oneself the blessings and rewards of the human or celestial realms, nor those of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas,
nor even those of the various provisional vehicles.

Abiding as a Bodhisattva, relying solely upon the Supreme Vehicle, one generates the bodhicitta with the vow that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may simultaneously attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
This awakened mind now generated is far removed from all natures, characteristics, aggregates, bases, and elements;
it is free from the grasping at subject and object, and all phenomena are equal in their selflessness, like space.

Emptiness. One's own mind is fundamentally unarisen; its emptiness is perfectly quiescent. Therefore, just as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have given rise to the great bodhicitta, I too give rise to it in this way.
For this reason, I pay homage with a sincere heart.
Next, I shall cause you all to resolve upon bodhicitta; listen attentively.
Even if a glowing iron wheel were to spin upon the crown of your heads, you must never, for the sake of such suffering, fall away from the resolve for bodhicitta.
Next, form the Bodhicitta-mudrā (the two hands joined hollowly in the shape of a lotus).
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. (The Master’s mudrā and mantra are as they should be known.
One should contemplate that the Buddha, the sentient beings, and one’s own mind are non-differentiated in three ways, and dissolve them within a single thought-instant.)
It becomes a vast lunar disc,
like that of the night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month.
At midnight, when there are no clouds, it is exceedingly pure and brilliant.
Equal to the expanse of space, one should visualize within the lunar disc a golden letter *A*, as fine as the tip of an autumn hair, neither existent nor non-existent.
At the time of such contemplation, one must not apply the faculty of conceptual cognition; above, there is no Buddha to be realized, and below, there are no sentient beings.
Sentient beings may be delivered. Within this, there is no practice to be cultivated; afflictions, bodhi, birth-and-death, and nirvāṇa are all utterly purified.

This is the great essential mystery. You should apply your mind well to it. Not only will it bring benefit to spirits and deities, but practitioners as well will soon attain realization within this very state.
(After the Master recites the mantra three times in unison with the assembly, he says:)
I have now brought forth the bodhicitta for you all. Sons of the Buddha, you should know that bodhicitta arises from great compassion;
it is the direct cause for attaining Buddhahood, the root of wisdom, and that which can destroy ignorance. It cannot be defiled or destroyed by afflictions or evil karma.
Next, I shall confer upon you the Samaya precepts;
having received the Buddha-precepts, you shall immediately enter the rank of all Buddhas. Once your status is equal to that of Great Enlightenment, you are truly the children of all Buddhas.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā (with both hands in the vajra-bond, the six fingers interlaced outwardly, and the thumbs and ring fingers extended like needles; recite the mantra).
Oṃ samayasattva vaṃ. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as follows:
one should visualize within the mudrā a white syllable *vaṃ* emitting great light that universally illuminates all sentient beings who have been invited.
Those sentient beings, as well as the Buddhas of the three times, receive this illumination. Regarding the precepts...
The *pāramitās* are simultaneously perfected as the wholesome dharmas of the *dharmadhātu*. Visualize them as light rays of flowing radiance that confer empowerment (*abhiṣeka*), filling his body.
His body becomes identical to Samantabhadra; seated upon a great lunar disc, he succeeds to the office of all Buddhas as their legitimate son.
Regarding this prior connection for opening the scripture, the Buddha told Ānanda: "If you wish to receive and uphold the method of bestowing food (*bali*), you must rely upon..."
Regarding the study of yoga: one must first generate the bodhicitta and receive the samaya vows before being fit to receive the transmission of this dharma;
these are the aforementioned mantras. There are many commentaries on the Tibetan version; students should examine them for themselves, as they will provide the necessary details.
I have now completed the conferral of the samaya precepts for you all. From this day forward, I shall enable you to enter the rank of the Tathāgata;
you are true sons of the Buddha, born through transformation from the Dharma, and have obtained a share of the Buddha-dharma.
"You sentient beings, both of the dark and the light realms— I now bestow upon you the food of nectar;
through the empowerment of the Dharma-power, it pervades the ten directions, causing each and every one of you to be fully satiated.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Tathāgata of Infinite Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance (right wing curved upward, fist clenched, [the thumb] at the level of the precept finger...).
The Dhyāna-pāramitā mudrā: the left palm faces upward with the five fingers extended.
Recite the secret mantra: Oṃ sarvadhātugata-ajvaloke vaṃ paravaṃ para sapara sapara hūṃ.
(The Master’s seal-mantra may be understood accordingly. The attendant takes water and sprinkles it into the bowls and the bucket. He then withdraws and sits in his original position.
The Master should snap his fingers with his right hand in a threatening manner to dispel the māras with his left hand, while reciting: *Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*.)
Recite three times. Ask: "What kind of demon is in your hand? Answer: "Because there are various corpse-insects (*śava-kṛmi*) within my hand, I must protect it.
Next, transform the hand into emptiness by reciting *Oṃ Khaṃ*, either once or three times. Ask: "What is the intention behind transforming this hand into emptiness?
Answer: "Because this hand is composed of the two kinds of impurities—red and white—I empty it so that it may become supreme."
[He is] the one whose hands are adorned with wondrous merit. Question: Since he has previously entered meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), he is himself a Bodhisattva;
for what reason does he now again dispatch Māra to transform space? Answer: This is the performance of a rite (*vidhi*). Did I not say above that this was so?
If you wish to know it now, it accords with the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, which says: After the World-Honored One had preached the *Ananta-artha-nirdeśa*, he entered the third [meditation].
He emitted light while in a state of meditative absorption, and again emitted light upon entering samādhi to open the precious stūpa. Is this not a case of confusion? No, it is not.
It is because one phenomenon is manifested through a single event; such is the ritual protocol of the Dharma. It is like the worldly etiquette for those who sacrifice in the ancestral temple:
they undergo fasting and purification, yet when they ascend the hall to perform the incense offering, they wash their hands once more. Why is this? It is for the sake of...
This expresses reverence. Now, once again, Māra is transformed into emptiness; this expresses the depth of compassion and the extremity of pity, as well as the intensity of one's resolve.
Then, in a single instant, a supreme and wondrous hand is suddenly formed.
From within the palm of that hand, a red syllable *Bhaṃ* emerges and transforms into a red lotus flower. Upon the flower, one visualizes a white syllable *Vaṃ*, which is a bindu.
From within, inexhaustible food and drink flow forth. Visualize that the water vessels before you all become *māgadha* measures.
Alternatively, visualize them adorned with the seven precious jewels, filled to the brim with exquisite and sublime foods and so forth.
Then, visualize that these seed-syllables flow forth inexhaustible food and drink, transforming and filling the entire *dharmadhātu*. Recite: Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ hūṃ.
Recite the four-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times, or forty-nine times; you should know for yourself when to do so. Next, recite the mantra for transforming food.
With each recitation, take food and drink from within the *bindu* and sprinkle it into the void.

"O sons of the Buddha, I have now performed the seal-mantra for you. I shall transform this single meal into immeasurable food, as vast as Mount Sumeru and equal in measure to the Dharma-realm, such that it can never be exhausted."
By the power of this mantra, transform the food into an ocean of milk; universally bestow it upon the hungry ghosts and others so that their bodies and minds are all fully satiated.

Again, bind the previous mudrā and recite the Ocean of Milk Mantra (with the right wing [hand] curved and the fist upright, the fingers of the *śīla* and *dhyāna* positions snapping together, and the left palm facing upward).
Extend the five fingers).
Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as before.
One should visualize nectar flowing forth from the *bindu* and take it up with the right hand to snap the fingers).
Sprinkled into the void like a torrential rain, wherever it reaches below, it immediately becomes a great river of ghee and curd. Question:
How can water and other substances from small vessels fill the entire Dharma-realm? Answer: Because the power of the mind is inconceivable;

how much more so when aided by the power of divine mantras, the visualization of seed-syllables (*bīja*), and even the secret empowerment of the Buddhas and the power of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
How could one not be able to transform the small into the great, or change the few into the many? Furthermore, let us borrow past events from the world as an analogy:
for instance, a single cup of wine, through the power of sorcery, can still be transformed into a drizzling rain;
how much more so, then, the inconceivable power of the divine? A practitioner must likewise focus their mind with undivided attention. Again, he asked: "Why?"

Therefore, he did not give them food or drink, but instead gave them water. [The questioner] asked: "Since those in the realm of hungry ghosts (*preta*) are mostly scorched by the fires of their karma, why does he now give them water?
Is it to douse and extinguish those karmic fires? The Buddha said: "Those hungry ghosts [have been so for] hundreds of thousands of myriads of kalpas."
They do not even hear the name of water, let alone obtain a drink. Furthermore, it is said that those ghosts, though standing on the banks of the Ganges, do not see the water;

even if they were to see it, it would turn into pus and blood. When they attempt to drink it, it enters their bellies and transforms into fierce flames, burning their hearts and abdomens with unbearable agony.
How tragic, how tragic! Therefore, I now offer this water as a gift, embodying this understanding.

This is my view. Furthermore, the Tibetan version states: *sru ba*, which is translated here as "water for the food offering" (*shuishishi*). Thus, we know that it originated from the offering of water.
It is a mistake that people today, being unaware of this, mostly use the water for the food offering [instead]. Moreover, in the present-day food offering, one does not exclusively use water;
rather, seven grains of rice are placed into the vessel to be offered universally throughout the ten directions. Therefore, do not harbor doubts regarding these matters.
Addressing all you sons of the Buddha: I have now performed this seal-mantra for you.

By the power of the empowerment of this seal-mantra, visualize that nectar flows forth from within the seal, forming an ocean of milk that pours into the entire dharmadhātu, universally rescuing all sentient beings such as yourselves and satisfying them to full repletion.
"You karmic-obstruction spirits, though you transform yourselves into fire, you cannot consume [this food]. Now, by reciting these secret words, you shall all be satiated with the Dharma-food.
Next, recite the mantra of the obstructing-giving spirits.
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ ca la mi daṃ sarvāpṛthivīya svāhā. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly;
one should extend the right wing [of the hand]. Visualize that within the palm there is the syllable *vaṃ*.
From the bindu, nectar flows out and descends from the left palm. Recite: Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ hūṃ.)
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, or twenty-one times. Then, the attendant may approach the Master, prostrate, take the pure flask, and exit the altar.
Slowly pouring the pure water down, when the Master reaches the point of chanting, he should visualize that the obstructing spirits and ghosts all kneel with their right knees on the ground.
The Master then visualizes himself as Avalokiteśvara, appearing before them all and bestowing nectar from the crown of their heads.
Enter [the mandala]. Extinguish the fires of their karma and attain coolness. Recite the mantra three times, snapping the fingers once for each recitation.
Recite the mantra three or seven times; this satisfies the obstructing spirits and others, causing them to rejoice. Snap the fingers once.
At that time, the practitioner shall take the vessel of nectar with the right hand, stand facing east, and pour it before the altar or upon clean ground. Or...
On a stone, or in a new, clean earthenware basin—also called an *ulambana* bowl—or on a raised platform;
or in a spring, pond, river, sea, or flowing stream. One must not pour it beneath a *ju-liu* (pomegranate) or peach tree, for the ghosts and spirits will be terrified.
One must not eat it. If food and drink are offered to the Vidyārājas and various devas within the altar of the Noble Assembly, they should be placed upon a living platform;
this is the fundamental method. When making offerings to the Buddhas and the Noble Assembly, it should be done at the fifth watch of the night, at dawn when the sun rises.

Regarding these times of offering: if following the ritual for spirits and ghosts (*preta*), it is fixed at the *hai* hour of the day; if following the ritual for humans, it is fixed at the time of their own meal.
According to the ritual of the *ācārya*, if performed during the midday meal, one may offer food, water, and so forth, consecrated by mantras throughout the entire day.

For birds, beasts, and aquatic creatures that fly through the air, there is no restriction regarding the specific time; one simply offers to them. If performing the *bali* offering for hungry ghosts (*preta-bali*), [the timing is as follows].
Regarding this Dharma: if one offers food to the hungry ghosts during the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m. or during the time of the midday meal, it will be a mere waste of effort and ultimately ineffective.
If one acts at an improper time, one’s offerings will be in vain; the spirits and ghosts will not receive the food.
To practice this without receiving it from a teacher invites calamity and brings about the offense of stealing the Dharma. This is according to the version from the Tripiṭaka.
O sons of the Buddhas, although beings are categorized by their kind and grouped by their nature, my giving is entirely unimpeded;
it is without high or low, equal and universal, making no distinction between enemy and kin.

Today, do not treat the humble with contempt because they are noble, nor oppress the weak because you are strong, nor obstruct the orphaned and the young so that they may not obtain food, thereby making the distribution unjust.
Transcending the Buddha’s compassionate aid, you must necessarily cherish one another, maintaining a thought like that of parents remembering their children.
Addressing the sons of the Buddha: "Each of you has parents, brothers, sisters, wives, children, kinsmen, good friends, and relatives.
Should there be circumstances that prevent them from coming, you, sons of the Buddha, must each regard them with compassion and love."
Each of you shall take food, drink, money, and goods, and bestow them upon one another in succession until all are fully satisfied and none lack anything.
This shall cause you to resolve upon the Way, forever leave the three miserable realms, and for long transcend the four torrents.

When you cast off this body, may you swiftly surpass the fruits of the Path. Furthermore, for your sake, I shall divide these pure foods into three portions: one portion I shall give to the aquatic creatures.

First, by bestowing [gifts] upon humans, they cause them to realize the emptiness of persons (*pudgala-śūnyatā*). Second, by bestowing [gifts] upon the flocks of beasts, they cause them to attain the tranquility of phenomena (*dharma-śānti*). Third, by bestowing [gifts] upon others in other regions, they cause those who receive consciousness and whose forms are molded [by karma] to be fully satisfied, thereby attaining the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Through the empowerment of divine mantras, may these pure dharma-foods be universally bestowed upon all spirits and deities as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
may they all be fully satiated, abandon stinginess and greed, swiftly escape the dark realms, and be reborn in the Pure Land.
Next, form the seal of universal offering (join the two palms straight together; bend the second joints of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers). Recite the mantra:
Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi sarva-ghasmarāya hūṃ. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as follows:

Answer: The previous actions were performed by distinguishing between the holy and the ordinary; therefore, the Three Jewels were honored first, followed by the distribution to the host of spirits.
Now, these are integrated through the equality of non-obstruction, such that the holy and the ordinary interpenetrate one another.
This is why they are universally offered as sustenance.

All you sons of the Buddha, the food and drink you have received from the past were all obtained through the sale of living beings in the human world—money, dried meats, wine, blood, flesh, raw and pungent odors, and foul-smelling, impure things. You who have today encountered this supreme occasion shall have the precepts permeate your bodies; thus, throughout past lives, you shall extensively serve the Buddhas.

Associate with virtuous friends and make offerings to the Triple Gem. By these causes and conditions, you shall encounter spiritual mentors (kalyāṇamitra), resolve to attain Bodhicitta, and vow to achieve Buddhahood, seeking no other fruit. Those who first attain the Way shall successively deliver one another.
Furthermore, I pray that you will constantly protect me day and night and fulfill my aspirations. By means of this offering of food...
May the merit thus generated be universally dedicated to all sentient beings of the *dharmadhātu*.

Together with all sentient beings, may this merit be entirely dedicated toward unexcelled *bodhi* and the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), so that no other fruit be sought. May they swiftly attain Buddhahood.

DHRĪḤ MAHĀMUDRĀ-MANTRA PATI SVĀHĀ (Recite this mantra for rebirth in the Pure Land three times.
This completes the empowerment, which further consists of two types: first, the perfection of the divine mantra.)
Second is the perfection of the roots of goodness. First, regarding the perfection of the mantra: the attendant should take flowers and rice and distribute them;
then the teacher and disciple chant the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī in unison, visualizing that they become seeds of light.

Having consecrated the flowers and rice, the attendant takes some on a small plate and scatters it outside. The teacher visualizes that spirits, ghosts, and other beings who come into contact with this light [are purified].
All shall attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss as those of the highest grade of the highest birth. The attendant pours out the food and pure water;

the teacher and disciple together recite the Six-Syllable Great Brightness Mantra one hundred and eight times. When this is finished, ring the bell and chant the Verse of the Dharma-Music for the Six Realms.
By virtue of this merit, for those sentient beings suffering in the hells, the mountains of knives and trees of swords shall all transform into wish-fulfilling trees;
the masses of fire and iron balls shall change into lotuses, becoming precious auspiciousness. Thus, they shall be liberated from the hells and attain perfect enlightenment.
May those sentient beings suffering as hungry ghosts, who receive these beneficial merits, have the flames of smoke burning their bodies quickly cooled.
May the nectar from within Avalokiteśvara’s hand naturally flow forth, providing eternal satiety and auspiciousness; may the hungry ghosts be liberated and attain perfect enlightenment.
By virtue of this merit, may those sentient beings who suffer as animals be forever freed from the agonies of slaughter, burning, boiling, and torment;
may they be liberated from being ridden and from ignorance, swiftly attain the auspiciousness of great wisdom, and, being released from animal existence, be able to achieve perfect enlightenment.
May those sentient beings in the human realm who endure suffering, by virtue of this merit, be born from the right side like Māyā;

may they possess the six sense faculties, forever be free from the eight difficulties, cultivate the auspiciousness of merit and wisdom, attain liberation in the human world, and be able to achieve perfect enlightenment.
May those asuras who suffer due to this lack of merit, who are arrogant, deranged, and crude, quickly become gentle and virtuous.
May their evil minds, characterized by envy, malice, and strife, be self-subdued and auspicious; may the asuras attain liberation and be able to achieve perfect enlightenment.
May those sentient beings who enjoy bliss in the heavens by virtue of this merit exert themselves with diligence toward sensual pleasures and swiftly give rise to the vast bodhicitta.
May their sorrows and sufferings in the heavens naturally end, and may they spontaneously experience joy, auspiciousness, and liberation within the heavens,
thereby attaining perfect enlightenment.

By virtue of this wholesome benefit, the Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas of the ten directions abandon the practices of the Four Noble Truths and the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination of the Hīnayāna,

and instead advance toward the Mahāyāna through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) and the six perfections (*pāramitā*). Cultivating the auspiciousness of the myriad practices, they attain liberation from the two vehicles and are able to achieve Perfect Enlightenment (*samyaksaṃbodhi*).
Those bodhisattvas of the first stage who possess courageous wisdom and receive this virtuous benefit will be adorned with a hundred merits; all their practices and vows will be fully perfected.

They will suddenly transcend the ten stages and attain the auspicious state of being "born only once more" before buddhahood. In the Mahāyāna, they will swiftly realize the ultimate attainment of perfect enlightenment.
Verse of Aspiration and Dedication:
Until I have realized Bodhi in this present life, May I never encounter internal or external obstacles, difficulties, or adverse conditions;
May I always meet with the most sublime and virtuous spiritual friends, And may all the wholesome deeds and practices I cultivate be swiftly fulfilled.
At the time of my final passing, may my consciousness be free from delusion regarding the Supreme Triple Gem;

May I be reborn before the Tathāgata in the Pure Land of the West, relying upon the radiance of the Sun of Wisdom to engage in hearing, contemplation, and cultivation; May I sever afflictions, realize the Truth, and compassionately regard all sentient beings.
The supreme Triple Gem can bestow upon others the merit of giving back what has been given;
all the various merits thus obtained are like magical illusions, and these illusions are like dream-visions. The three spheres are empty in essence, and this emptiness is utterly pure.
Supreme Triple Gem (Auspicious Verse):
May there be auspiciousness by day and auspiciousness by night! May the Guru come to grant his grace!
May there be constant auspiciousness throughout the six periods of day and night! May all the Triple Gems come to grant their grace!
Auspicious at all times, may the Protectors of the Dharma always provide guardianship.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the Western Quarter, to the great Bodhisattvas, and to the assembly of holy ones gathered like the ocean.

We pray that for all beings within the Dharma-realm, both living and deceased, their offenses may be equally eliminated and they may be reborn together in the Pure Land. May this be dedicated toward unsurpassed Buddha-bodhi. (Strike the chime.)
(As stated below):

Seeing and hearing are like illusory cataracts; the three realms are like flowers in the sky. When hearing is restored, the cataracts of the sense-roots are removed, dust is eliminated, and awakening becomes perfectly pure.

I humbly submit that the True Source is profound and tranquil; thus, the nature of sin is fundamentally empty. Yet the ocean of suffering is vast and deep, its waves of delusion surging without ceasing.
Due to the karmic retributions of sentient beings, they remain submerged and transmigrate through long kalpas, enduring the torments of hell for eternity.
Reborn within the realm of hungry ghosts, they suffer from perpetual hunger and emptiness, with no prospect of liberation in sight.
How could there be a path for transcendence and elevation without relying upon the compassionate vows of the Tathāgata? How else could the inverted suspension of the evil realms be resolved?
By reciting mantras and chanting the true teachings, he bestows the Dharma-food of ambrosia; by lighting lamps as precious torches, he illuminates the dark paths of the netherworld.

May all wandering beings in delusion together transcend to the Land of Ultimate Bliss. By means of the merit universally bestowed here at today’s site of enlightenment, I dedicate it to the Great Being Flaming Mouth (Yamen Dashi), who presides over the thirty-six classes of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of immeasurable, boundless Ganges Rivers within the Iron Ring Mountains.
I pray that from the beginningless kalpas until this present life, they may be liberated from their karmic obstructions.
Melted away! Sins and transgressions are purified and cleansed. The boiling cauldrons transform into lotus ponds of the eight virtues;
the interlacing flames of the furnaces become fragrant canopies of the seven treasures. The sword-trees all become jade trees, and the mountain of blades entirely becomes a mountain of jewels.
The iron beds throughout the world manifest as Dharma-thrones of Bodhi; the molten copper in the cauldrons transforms into nectar.
The Supreme Nectar: Former creditors meet once more, and both are granted liberation; enemies from kalpas past assemble together, each finding ultimate ease.
The Lord of Hell arouses compassion, and the Underworld Officials uphold virtue. Parents from many lifetimes pass from this point into the Holy and transcend the mundane;
relatives and kin from successive generations receive grace and obtain blessings from this moment on. The five signs of decay no longer appear in the heavens, and among humans...
The four marks are all empty. Asuras abandon and exhaust their hearts of anger; those in the hells find relief from all suffering and affliction;
hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges transform their feverish distress into coolness. Beings of the ten realms leave the path of delusion and ascend to the shore of enlightenment.
May all sentient beings throughout this land, other lands, and immeasurable lands alike together realize the True and Eternal. This...
May all sentient beings throughout this world, other worlds, and infinite worlds without end attain the Buddha-way together.

May the four debts of gratitude be universally repaid, may those in the three realms of existence be equally sustained, and may all beings within the dharma-realm together perfect the wisdom of all modes.
In the Buddha, the True Dharma, and the Sangha of Bodhisattvas, I take refuge until I reach enlightenment.
By all the roots of virtue I have cultivated, may I attain Buddhahood for the benefit of sentient beings.
May all that is mundane and supramundane be accomplished according to my wishes; may it be accomplished according to my wishes.
Relying reverently upon the Yoga teachings, I establish this dharma assembly; may it be universally bestowed upon all sentient beings so that they may together attain the Buddha-way.

Next, perform the seal of the perfect completion for the dismissal (with both hands in vajra-fists, hooking the two middle fingers [forefingers] together). At this point, recite the mantra three times.

The roots of goodness are perfected. Question: Since the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have already departed, they no longer appear; who then acts as witness? Answer:
This reveals that in coming there is truly no coming, and in departing there is truly no departing. The Triple Gem abides eternally in the world.
Furthermore, as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* states: "The stupa of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna remains as it was.
When the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara arrives, the Buddha Prabhūtaratna and his stupa have never been absent. If he is invited, he truly comes; if he is sent away, he truly departs.
How is this different from ghosts and spirits? Let the student reflect upon this, and further recite the hundred-syllable mantra of Vajrasattva.

[From] the *Pretasūtra*.

The meaning of "yoga" is taken here as "correspondence," meaning that only when the three—body, speech, and mind—are unified with sincerity does benefit arise. "Mind" refers to the gate of visualization (*vipaśyanā*);
"body and speech" refer to mantra and mudrā. As for whether the master’s visualization was performed according to the ritual at that time, it remains uncertain.

It is easy to inquire about this, yet the mantras and mudrās are clearly manifest; nevertheless, there are significant differences and similarities regarding what is perceived by the ears and eyes, which has caused considerable doubt among later students.
Upon investigating the origins and developments, it appears that because the lineages of transmission were not derived from a single source, they have consequently been circulated together.

The various editions of this sutra differ so vastly that they are as disparate as heaven and earth; their contradictions are so numerous that one knows not which to follow—a truly lamentable state of affairs.
